description:
FILED s535a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from a span-port probe (scratch/s535a/pr/p16.pl).  PRE-EXISTING and LOUD on both main 06a4b8ba and the s535a tree.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my ($u, @v) = (1, 2, 3);
    package Foo;
    print "u=$u v=@v\n";

perl:              u=1 v=2 3
main / s535a:      Transpile failed: Parser2 TODO: my-lexical 'v' (canon @v) spans a package boundary

WHY: the span renamer promotes a CONTAINER only from a single-container declaration (`my @v` / `my %h`, the facts' container_decl, identity-only W10-ext-3); a container inside a LIST declaration is never offered, so it stays unpromoted and the checker (now Pl::Binder::spans' answer, s535a) refuses the file.  The scalar of the same list (`$u`) is promoted.  The same holds for a container in a chained declaration (`my @c = my @d = (1)`) and an embedded one -- since s535a those are refused LOUDLY (before s535a the chained / embedded ones were a SILENT wrong: the old checker never saw them).

FIX DIRECTION: offer list-declaration containers (the facts' mlist_decl entries with an @/% canon) to the container path, identity-only as today; the mixed renamed/unrenamed list-decl lowering already exists (the promoter's mlist path).  Measure first: 0 files in the gate-SET populations die with this message today.

=== DONE (s536e) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, generation v2-12900; commit 23baa13b).  `_span_rename_containers` offers the containers of a LIST declaration (the facts' `mlist_decl` entries with an `@`/`%` canon) exactly as a single-container `my @v` -- identity only, the same file-uniqueness / #470 / blockform conditions; the mixed promoted/unpromoted list lowering already existed.  Probed (scratch/s536e/pr/m3*.pl): `my ($u, @v)`, `my (%h, $s)`, `my ($r, %s)` beside `our ($p, @q)`, `my (@a, @b)` read by a later section's sub, a loop that pushes + a slice + `$#v` -- tree = perl.  Residue (still refused, loud): a chained container `my @c = my @d`, a container canon declared twice (`my ($x, %h); { my %h }`) -> #4662; an exception-named container -> #4661.  Guard span-binder-01.t rows 30-32 (fail on the base).  The gate-SET scan over both populations (638 files) is IDENTICAL: no file there died with the message.
subject: A container inside a LIST (or chained / embedded) `my` declaration used in a later `package` section is refused LOUDLY ("spans a package boundary") -- the span renamer offers only single-container declarations (pre-existing)
